duel.summary: Built the deterministic 1v1 duel as pure integer code. packages/content/src/moves holds the input bits, zod schemas and validators (the move timing reuses moveTimingSchema), the Duelist moveset (jab, heavy mid, low sweep and throw take their timing objects from baselineFrameBudgets; launcher, anti-air, advancing thrust and counter slash are the worker's choice), the §7 rules, the arena, MOVESET_VERSION 'duelist-1' and the input-log schema. packages/simulation/src/duel holds the state, stepDuel (inputs, then detection against the start-of-frame state, then same-frame interactions, then simultaneous apply, then movement, then stamina and result), boxes, snapshotDuel/restoreDuel, replayDuel/traceDuel/sliceDuelInputLog and createDuelInputLog. Subpath exports @pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel and @pirate-sea-race/content/moves follow the existing pattern, and each package has a postbuild that imports its subpath from dist/ without the source condition (it exits 1 when the source condition sends it to src/). docs/duel.md is written. Tests: 47 rule tests (round, timeout, overtime, double KO, a KO on the final frame, simultaneous hits, movement, walls, pushboxes, guard levels, throws with escape window, clash and strike priority, stamina costs, regeneration and guard break, combo scaling and cap, the 4-frame buffer, heavy mid -12 punished by a jab in the corner at max range and midscreen), 10 determinism, rollback, version and symmetry tests (frame-by-frame mirror with slots swapped; a one-sub-pixel wall asymmetry was confirmed to fail it), and 40 content validator tests. Checks run in this worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (183 passed), npm run test:integration (14 passed), npm run build (exit 0; both postbuild self-checks and the build smoke test passed). No commits were made; only owned paths changed.
open_assumptions: Counter slash is a reversal: strikes pass through its whole 8-frame startup; no parry/counter stance (that overlaps deferred Observation Haki).
Up + down held together is also neutral, like left + right (§8 names only horizontal).

Guard break replaces the blockstun with 30 frames of stagger from the breaking frame and sets stamina to 30; after a broken heavy mid the attacker is only +2, while a broken jab is punishable (tested).
'An active strike beats a throw' is read literally: a fighter whose strike hitbox is active that frame cannot be grabbed, even if the strike whiffs.
Throw escape counts only presses after the grab (the buffer is cleared at the grab): the window is grab+1..grab+10, and the throw lands on grab+11; a throw causes a 30-frame non-hittable knockdown.
Frame convention: startup = frames before the first active frame; blockstun and hitstun include the contact frame, so advantage = blockstun - active - recovery.
Jab hitstun 24 (+9 on hit) so that jabs link and the five-hit cap is reachable; balance (15-25% combos) is untuned.
Pushback is applied instantly; fighters can jump over each other (80 px pushbox); there is no air guard and there are no air attacks.
DuelState.rng is seeded and carried but no rule draws from it yet.
scripts/smoke-build.ts and packages/test-tools are unchanged, as decided; the new subpaths are proven by the postbuild scripts only.

findings.message: Pushbox separation has a slot bias in an edge case. packages/simulation/src/duel/step.ts:417 breaks an x tie with `aLeft = a.x < b.x || (a.x === b.x && a.facing === 1)`. When both fighters share an x and face the same way (possible after a cross-up, because only a free fighter turns), slot 0 is always pushed left. In the mirrored duel, the mirror of slot 0 is also pushed left instead of right, so the outcome depends on which slot a player has. The symmetry test's scripted exchange never reaches this state. A slot-neutral tie-break (for example, one based on each fighter's own facing or a previous-frame order kept in state) would close it.
findings.requirement: the outcome never depends on which player is first

findings.message: A guard break sets stamina to 30 (step.ts:289, `stamina: Math.min(rules.maxStamina, rules.guardBreakStaminaRestore)`) instead of adding 30. A break only happens below the block cost (at most 24 stamina), so this gives 30 where an additive reading gives 30 to 54. docs/duel.md and the worker's open assumptions state this reading, so it is not hidden, but it is a balance-relevant interpretation of the spec's wording and the operator should confirm it.
findings.requirement: a guard break staggers 30 frames and restores 30 stamina

findings.message: restoreDuel (packages/simulation/src/duel/snapshot.ts:16-26) checks only movesetVersion, a non-negative integer frame and a two-element fighters array before copying. A snapshot with a missing or malformed fighter field (for example no `buffer`, or an unknown `action` or `phase`) is accepted and fails later inside stepDuel (a TypeError on `fighter.buffer[button]`) or silently diverges. It is the documented entry point for wire checkpoints, so validating the full state shape at restore (for example with a zod schema) would make bad checkpoints fail where they enter.

The moveset validator's 'no free opening hit' check (packages/content/src/moves/schema.ts:923-927) compares startGap only with the static hitbox reach plus the hurtbox reach. It ignores a move's `advance` (the advancing thrust moves 64 sub-pixels a frame through startup and active frames). Current data passes: the thrust reaches about 2400 sub-pixels against a start gap of 3072, and a test confirms that nothing connects from the start positions. A future data change could still start fighters within reach without the validator noticing.
findings.requirement: A zod validator rejects impossible data

findings.message: packages/simulation/src/duel/duel.test.ts:327 'decides a guard break from the stamina held at the start of the frame' only probes the cost threshold (stamina 25 vs 24 against a heavy). Both runs start from createDuelState with staminaIdle 0, so the block on frame 19 happens long before the 60-frame regeneration delay. Stamina therefore has only one possible value during that frame. The test would still pass if step.ts applied regeneration (step 6) before the block cost (step 4), or read stamina after any other in-frame change. No test sets up a contact frame on which a regeneration tick lands, for example stamina 24 with staminaIdle chosen so that the tick falls on the block frame, and asserts that the guard still breaks. The implementation reads start-of-frame stamina (react() uses fighter.stamina before the regeneration pass), but no test checks this ordering.
findings.requirement: Stamina costs and guard breaks of the frame are computed from start-of-frame stamina.

findings.message: The postbuild self-checks in packages/simulation/package.json and packages/content/package.json ran and passed on the candidate (build log: both subpaths load from dist/). Only their success path has run. No test or captured evidence shows either script failing when the subpath resolves outside dist/ or the module exports nothing. The worker's claim that the script exits 1 under the source condition is not in any verification packet. The failure logic is a short inline script that can be checked by reading it, so the risk is low.
findings.requirement: each of the two packages gets a `postbuild` script that imports its new subpath from `dist/` without the source condition and fails when it resolves elsewhere or exports nothing

inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: duel-core

From the operator session of 2026-09-24 (slice planning after the skeleton merged into `main`), revised after design challenge attempt 1 of duel-core-001 by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish the run.

## Decisions

- Scope is the pure duel simulation only (slice 1 of the plan). Networking, the arena client and the duel room are the next feature, `duel-online`, which builds against this feature's API from `main`. The API therefore has to be usable without changes: a step function, a snapshot that is plain data, and a pure replay function.
- One lane (`duel`). Duel rules and move data are too coupled to split, and a split lane would fail its isolated typecheck against the other's types.
- Only the Duelist kit. Fruit kits (§9) come with the content slice; the Duelist's two specials are the advancing thrust and the counter slash.
- Haki abilities (§10: Armament, Observation parry, Resolve finisher) and the Haki meter are deferred. The spike's exit (§18: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit, reconnect) doesn't need them, and they add balance work before the core is proven.
- Units: integer sub-pixels, 16 sub-pixels per arena pixel. Positions, velocities, gravity and hitboxes are integers; hitboxes and hurtboxes are axis-aligned rectangles relative to the fighter's origin and facing.
- The code lives in new directories behind subpath exports (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves`), so this feature edits no existing file. `world-sea` runs at the same time on the rest of the repository, and the two branches must merge without conflicts.
- No browser check: nothing is rendered. The policy's checks are typecheck, unit, integration (unchanged, to prove nothing broke) and build.
- Proving the build output (challenge P1): `scripts/smoke-build.ts` hard-codes the existing exports and `scripts/` is not this lane's (the policy can't change without a new run, and `world-sea` owns `scripts/`). So each of the two packages proves its own new subpath with a `postbuild` script that imports it from `dist/` without the source condition. Adding the two subpaths to `smoke-build.ts` is left for the merge or a later feature.
- The replay runner is a pure `replayDuel` in `packages/simulation/src/duel`, with the log's zod schema in `packages/content/src/moves` (challenge P2). `packages/test-tools` would need a new dependency on `simulation`, and so a lockfile change, and the lockfile belongs to `world-sea` in this parallel pair. `duel-online` can wrap `replayDuel` in `test-tools` later. This departs from §17's "test-tools: replay runner" for now.
- Simplified collision data (challenge's simpler alternative): one hitbox per move for its whole active phase and one hurtbox per stance. Per-frame timelines wait until playtests need them.
- Same-frame rules the spec leaves open, decided here: detect everything against start-of-frame state and apply together; throw against throw breaks both with no damage; an active strike beats a throw in startup or active; stamina and guard breaks use start-of-frame stamina. A mirrored-players symmetry test guards order independence.
- The duel input carries held directions as separate left/right/up/down bits, so the step resolves both-horizontal to neutral (§8) and `duel-online`'s adapter passes keys through unchanged.
- The four §8 baseline moves take their timings from `baselineFrameBudgets` and reuse `moveTimingSchema`, and the duel state records `MOVESET_VERSION` so a snapshot is never replayed against other move data.

## Assumptions

- The arena is one plane with two walls and a floor; its width is content data. There's no stage hazard and no ring-out.
- A duel input per player per frame is one bit field: held directions (left, right, up, down) and buttons (light, heavy, special one, special two, dash), as §8 maps keys. Keyboard mapping is client work.
- Frame data for moves outside §8's table (launcher, anti-air, the two specials) is the worker's choice within §7's ranges, documented in the move data.
- `hashState` from `packages/simulation` is reused for duel state, which also holds the duel's own frame counter and generator state if it needs one.
- The duel starts both fighters at fixed positions, facing each other, with full health and stamina, as §6 requires ("no free opening hit").

## Deferred

- Haki meter and abilities (§10), fruit kits (§9), focus scrolls.
- Networking, prediction and reconciliation, the input delay policy, reconnect: `duel-online`.
- Rendering, animation, the duel HUD and control remapping: `duel-online`.
- Hosting the duel inside `MatchRoom`, reservations, transitions and theft: `encounters-theft`.

concerns.message: The heavy-mid punish test can pass without proving anything. If the heavy is blocked point-blank, any jab reaches. At the heavy's maximum range, the defender's jab only reaches if jab reach ≥ heavy hitbox reach + block pushback, measured hurtbox edge to hurtbox edge. The acceptance says 'at the spacing a blocked heavy actually leaves' but does not say which contact distance to use.
concerns.consequence: If the worker tests at close range, the design can ship a −12 heavy that can't be punished at tip range. §8's promised 'punish opportunity' then fails the first time duel-online plays it, and pushback, reach and MOVESET_VERSION all have to be retuned.

concerns.message: Throw is J+K together, but light is J alone. If a jab starts on the frame J is pressed, a keyboard player who hits K 1–2 frames later gets a jab, not a throw. Rollover rarely puts both keys on the same 60 Hz frame. The plan defines a 4-frame buffer but no chord leniency, such as 'a jab in its first N startup frames becomes a throw when heavy arrives'.
concerns.consequence: Scripted-input unit tests put J and K on the same frame, so they pass. Online, throws are nearly impossible to input. §18's 'throw' spike exit fails in duel-online, and the fix changes step semantics and move data after snapshots and replays are already in use.

concerns.message: MOVESET_VERSION is a hand-maintained constant. The refusal check passes silently when someone edits frame data or hitboxes and forgets to bump it. §17 asks for a content hash.
concerns.consequence: Old snapshots or replay logs replay against changed move data without being refused, and hashes diverge with no clear error. Rollback verification by duel-online is then untrustworthy.

concerns.message: The mirrored symmetry test is only as strong as its scripted exchange. Tie-breaks keyed to slot break order independence while a mild script still passes. Examples: splitting an odd pushbox overlap between fighters, the facing choice when both x values are equal (cross-ups), and which fighter a wall clamp moves first.
concerns.consequence: A slot-dependent rule survives into duel-online. There it looks like a desync or an unfair trade in exactly the jump-over or corner cases that §19's latency tests exercise.

concerns.message: The postbuild self-check can only live inline in package.json or under src/duel. A .ts self-check in src/duel is typechecked with lib es2024 and types [], so `process` and `import.meta.resolve` are untyped. It would also be compiled into dist and scanned by the purity test.
concerns.consequence: Typecheck or build fails, or a script ships inside the pure package's dist. Using `node --input-type=module -e` in the package.json script (or a .mjs file) avoids both.

concerns.message: replayDuel lives in simulation, but the log's zod schema is in content, and simulation's package.json only depends on content. If simulation imports zod directly, it only works through hoisting (a phantom dependency). Validation must go through a function exported from @pirate-sea-race/content/moves.
concerns.consequence: Adding zod to simulation's deps would touch the lockfile, which world-sea owns, and cause a merge conflict. A phantom import breaks under a stricter installer.

concerns.message: 'A strike whose hitbox is active beats a throw in startup or active' doesn't say whether the strike must actually overlap the thrower's hurtbox. A whiffing active strike shouldn't cancel a connecting throw.
concerns.consequence: If the literal reading is implemented, an out-of-range active jab makes the fighter throw-proof. That breaks 'throws beat guard' play and would need a rule change plus a MOVESET_VERSION/state change later.

concerns.message: hashState does two BigInt multiplies per UTF-16 unit. Hashing the full duel state every frame for 3,600+ frames in several tests (rollback, replay, symmetry) can take seconds each.
concerns.consequence: Unit tests near Vitest's 5 s default timeout become flaky in the verifier. Hash at checkpoints, or compare canonicalize() strings per frame, and hash only at the end.

challenge.simpler_alternative:
Keep the plan's scope, but make order independence hold by construction instead of relying on a test. Structure the step as phases over a frozen start-of-frame state:
(1) Resolve inputs per fighter: neutral on both horizontals, buffer, and chord leniency for throws.
(2) Compute each fighter's intended action.
(3) Detect with one pure `resolveContact(start, attackerSlot)` called for slot 0 and slot 1, both reading only `start`.
(4) Merge the two result records with slot-free rules: throw vs throw, strike vs throw, simultaneous KO, and stamina from start values.
(5) Apply movement, pushback and wall clamps using position-based, not slot-based, tie-breaks.
The symmetry test then checks the construction rather than having to find a bug. Make MOVESET_VERSION pair with a test that pins hashState of the move table, so editing data without bumping the version fails CI.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before writing any rule code, spend 20 minutes on a scratch unit test in packages/content/src/moves that does only the integer arithmetic for the §8 heavy mid, blocked on its first active frame at its maximum reach. Use the chosen hurtbox widths, the heavy's hitbox, the block pushback and the jab's hitbox. Assert that the defender's jab, started when blockstun ends, overlaps the attacker's hurtbox by jab startup frame 7, which is within the 12-frame window. In the same sitting, script J on frame f and K on frame f+1 and f+2, and decide whether that should give a throw. If the tip-range numbers force a jab that outranges the heavy, or if throws need chord leniency, that changes the move data and the input-buffer design before anything depends on them.

# Task: duel

## Goal

Build the deterministic 1v1 duel simulation of §7 and §8 as pure code: two fighters with the Duelist kit in one single-plane arena, stepped at 60 Hz from per-frame inputs, with snapshots that restore and replay exactly. This is the core that the combat spike (`duel-online`) will put online, and that the match room will later host as a duel object (§14). No rendering and no networking.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §7 (fighting system), §8 (controls and frame budgets), §15 ("Authoritative prediction policy": snapshots, restore, replay), §14 ("Match and duel boundaries") and §19 ("Combat determinism"). §9 describes the Duelist kit; §10's Haki abilities are deferred (see `decisions.md`).
- Read `docs/architecture.md` and the existing pure packages: `packages/simulation` (integer state, `hashState`, the seeded generator in `random.ts`, `fixed.ts`), `packages/content` (`frameBudgets.ts` already holds §8's baseline table with a zod validator) and `tests/unit/purity.test.ts`, which also scans any new directory under the pure packages.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build` (which ends with `scripts/smoke-build.ts`). It reads test counts from Vitest's summary; `tests/reporters/testSummary.ts` also prints them.
- Another feature (`world-sea`) runs at the same time on the rest of the repository. Stay inside your owned paths so the two merge cleanly.

## Constraints

- Owned paths only: `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `packages/content/src/moves`, `packages/simulation/package.json` and `packages/content/package.json` (only for the subpath exports and the `postbuild` self-check below) and `docs/duel.md`. # Decisions: duel-core

From the operator session of 2026-09-24 (slice planning after the skeleton merged into `main`), revised after design challenge attempt 1 of duel-core-001 by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish the run.

## Decisions

- Scope is the pure duel simulation only (slice 1 of the plan). Networking, the arena client and the duel room are the next feature, `duel-online`, which builds against this feature's API from `main`. The API therefore has to be usable without changes: a step function, a snapshot that is plain data, and a pure replay function.
- One lane (`duel`). Duel rules and move data are too coupled to split, and a split lane would fail its isolated typecheck against the other's types.
- Only the Duelist kit. Fruit kits (§9) come with the content slice; the Duelist's two specials are the advancing thrust and the counter slash.
- Haki abilities (§10: Armament, Observation parry, Resolve finisher) and the Haki meter are deferred. The spike's exit (§18: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit, reconnect) doesn't need them, and they add balance work before the core is proven.
- Units: integer sub-pixels, 16 sub-pixels per arena pixel. Positions, velocities, gravity and hitboxes are integers; hitboxes and hurtboxes are axis-aligned rectangles relative to the fighter's origin and facing.
- The code lives in new directories behind subpath exports (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves`), so this feature edits no existing file. `world-sea` runs at the same time on the rest of the repository, and the two branches must merge without conflicts.
- No browser check: nothing is rendered. The policy's checks are typecheck, unit, integration (unchanged, to prove nothing broke) and build.
- Proving the build output (challenge P1): `scripts/smoke-build.ts` hard-codes the existing exports and `scripts/` is not this lane's (the policy can't change without a new run, and `world-sea` owns `scripts/`). So each of the two packages proves its own new subpath with a `postbuild` script that imports it from `dist/` without the source condition. Adding the two subpaths to `smoke-build.ts` is left for the merge or a later feature.
- The replay runner is a pure `replayDuel` in `packages/simulation/src/duel`, with the log's zod schema in `packages/content/src/moves` (challenge P2). `packages/test-tools` would need a new dependency on `simulation`, and so a lockfile change, and the lockfile belongs to `world-sea` in this parallel pair. `duel-online` can wrap `replayDuel` in `test-tools` later. This departs from §17's "test-tools: replay runner" for now.
- Simplified collision data (challenge's simpler alternative): one hitbox per move for its whole active phase and one hurtbox per stance. Per-frame timelines wait until playtests need them.
- Same-frame rules the spec leaves open, decided here: detect everything against start-of-frame state and apply together; throw against throw breaks both with no damage; an active strike beats a throw in startup or active; stamina and guard breaks use start-of-frame stamina. A mirrored-players symmetry test guards order independence.
- The duel input carries held directions as separate left/right/up/down bits, so the step resolves both-horizontal to neutral (§8) and `duel-online`'s adapter passes keys through unchanged.
- The four §8 baseline moves take their timings from `baselineFrameBudgets` and reuse `moveTimingSchema`, and the duel state records `MOVESET_VERSION` so a snapshot is never replayed against other move data.

## Assumptions

- The arena is one plane with two walls and a floor; its width is content data. There's no stage hazard and no ring-out.
- A duel input per player per frame is one bit field: held directions (left, right, up, down) and buttons (light, heavy, special one, special two, dash), as §8 maps keys. Keyboard mapping is client work.
- Frame data for moves outside §8's table (launcher, anti-air, the two specials) is the worker's choice within §7's ranges, documented in the move data.
- `hashState` from `packages/simulation` is reused for duel state, which also holds the duel's own frame counter and generator state if it needs one.
- The duel starts both fighters at fixed positions, facing each other, with full health and stamina, as §6 requires ("no free opening hit").

## Deferred

- Haki meter and abilities (§10), fruit kits (§9), focus scrolls.
- Networking, prediction and reconciliation, the input delay policy, reconnect: `duel-online`.
- Rendering, animation, the duel HUD and control remapping: `duel-online`.
- Hosting the duel inside `MatchRoom`, reservations, transitions and theft: `encounters-theft`.

Checks run in this worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (183 passed), npm run test:integration (14 passed), npm run build (exit 0; both postbuild self-checks and the build smoke test passed). No commits were made; only owned paths changed.
open_assumptions: Counter slash is a reversal: strikes pass through its whole 8-frame startup; no parry/counter stance (that overlaps deferred Observation Haki).
Up + down held together is also neutral, like left + right (§8 names only horizontal).

Guard break replaces the blockstun with 30 frames of stagger from the breaking frame and sets stamina to 30; after a broken heavy mid the attacker is only +2, while a broken jab is punishable (tested).
'An active strike beats a throw' is read literally: a fighter whose strike hitbox is active that frame cannot be grabbed, even if the strike whiffs.
Throw escape counts only presses after the grab (the buffer is cleared at the grab): the window is grab+1..grab+10, and the throw lands on grab+11; a throw causes a 30-frame non-hittable knockdown.
Frame convention: startup = frames before the first active frame; blockstun and hitstun include the contact frame, so advantage = blockstun - active - recovery.
Jab hitstun 24 (+9 on hit) so that jabs link and the five-hit cap is reachable; balance (15-25% combos) is untuned.
Pushback is applied instantly; fighters can jump over each other (80 px pushbox); there is no air guard and there are no air attacks.
DuelState.rng is seeded and carried but no rule draws from it yet.
scripts/smoke-build.ts and packages/test-tools are unchanged, as decided; the new subpaths are proven by the postbuild scripts only.
